sn6.13:1.1: The Buddha taught Ānanda there ([an5.114]()). It lay to the west of Rājagaha on the road from Varanasi. Once, arriving there from Varanasi, the Buddha allowed porridge ([pli-tv-kd6:24.1.1](), cf. [an5.207]()). At [pli-tv-kd2:12.1.1](), Mahākassapa was swept away in a river while returning from Andhakavinda. That river is identified by the commentary as the Serpentine, but that is usually said to be the Panchane, which lies to the east of Rājagaha. Perhaps the river near Andhakavinda was, rather, the Paimar, which lies about three hours walk to the west of Rājagaha.
